title: Henry Allen's band and brass band instrumentation
summary: Morris played plenty in Henry Allen's Algiers band; the group describes its size, no saxophones, the tenor horn, piccolo and flute.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Do you remember the old, real old bands like Excelsior band? Do you remember Henry Allen's band across the river? Oh, I played with him plenty. Oh, you did?
Yes, I played with him plenty.
Before Lil' Allen left, yeah.
Yeah.
You know, he used to play with us. He was in short pants then. Yeah, Henry Allen. And he kept that band for years and years.
How many musicians did they have in Henry Allen's band?
I don't know. Sometime he'd be short-handed, you know. Them fellas, they just go out anyhow.
Would he have as many as, say, 20?
No, not that many.
What would be the full band?
Yeah, well...
How many trumpets? How many trombones?
Well, they'd only used two trombones and three trumpets. You see, the fellas done got so now they cut down on them band.
Yeah. stuff
Yeah, they cut down.
Did they use saxophones those days?
Yes, they didn't use saxophones.
But what'd they have then? Instead of saxophones.
They'd have a, wait, I'm going to tell you. One of them little, little, little horns like that. A tenor, they call it. Because Louis Kepin used to play one of them things, you know. Alto.
Alto.
Yeah.
The peck horn, they ever call them that?
Yeah, they used to have a flute. But you don't catch everybody playing them flute now, you know. No. Thing with the hole there.
Like a piccolo.
Yeah, like a piccolo. You don't catch many people play that now. They had one or two people here playing them things.
Did they use the big clarinet, the B flat, or the little short one?
In the little short one, yeah.
Would they use those flutes in the street?
Yeah, they used to use that in the street.
How long were they about?
It's about that long.
About 14 inches or something, a little over a foot.
Yes. That thing was loud, too, when you could play.
Let's see, if somebody I remember could play that thing, I just remember who it is.
But you could hear that thing louder than you do the cornet. Yeah.
